page: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadsv7 family, virtualized on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. It provides 48 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The cache subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, with instruction set support for AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16 extensions), AVX-VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI.

The instance is equipped with 192 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:4 virtual CPU to memory ratio (4 GB per vCPU). Direct storage is provisioned via an integrated 2,832 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by support for remote Azure Premium Storage. The server does not contain a discrete GPU. In benchmark evaluations, the D48ads_v7 registers top-tier execution, scoring 2,737.0 in Geekbench single-core and 24,148.0 in Geekbench multi-core. In-memory data throughput tests show 76.88 million operations per second on Redis SET operations, alongside 41.21 GB/sec single-threaded gzip compression.

Resource allocation delivers qualitative cost efficiency by bundling substantial local NVMe disk capacity directly with balanced compute and memory, eliminating extra external storage overhead for temporary data sets. The memory subsystem maintains uncached read speeds of 157.02 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 94.13 GB/sec. Because local NVMe disks are ephemeral, persistent storage needs rely on separate network attachments. The D48ads_v7 is matched for large relational databases, in-memory caching platforms, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and CI/CD pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine from the Dadsv7 series, featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs on a 24-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it contains 192 GB of system memory, matching a standard 4 GB per vCPU distribution, alongside 2,832 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The processor incorporates modern vector instruction extensions including AVX-512 and AVX-VNNI, with no discrete GPU included. Benchmark measurements show top-tier processing power, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 24,148.0 and Redis performance of 76.88 million operations per second. The instance provides balanced cost efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads needing high-speed local scratch space without auxiliary storage provisions. It is suited for relational database management systems, distributed caching tiers, automated build systems, and static web serving.
